items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Eddie West, who lived on Hathaway Street and with whom I used to draw pictures of fine looking automobiles, and many of the other boys that were in my gang.

ctx.x: Another time a pal and I were walking along the pike and we saw some farmers killing hogs, so we went over to see if we could do something and one of the wise guys said, 'yes, can you dance?' I said no I could not dance and he said, 'Well, I'll make you dance,' and he started to shoot at my feet with the rifle he was using to kill hogs. I didn't move and he was so angry that he said "get off this farm before I kill you". We left but he was the one who had lost face.

Some months later my father decided to go back to Cincinnati and that was very pleasing to me because the only boy around me on the farm with Aunt Amanda was her son Tom and I was happy at the thought of seeing Eddie Partridge, Eddie West, who lived on Hathaway Street and with whom I used to draw pictures of fine looking automobiles, and many of the other boys that were in my gang.

We lived on the 5th Street between Mound and Cutter Street over an undertaker parlor. The name of the undertaker was Mr. Copeland. When we lived on Barr Street, the Coplands lived across the street from me and I used to make candy-spending money from Mrs. Copland by watering her lawn in the summer and shoveling coal into her cellar in the winter.
